did.abstract: Paul A. Fino was a United States Representative from the Bronx, New York and this collection contains records related to his time in Congress.
did.physloc: The materials are located onsite in the department.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Paul A. Fino was a U.S. Representative for the Bronx, New York. Fino was born in New York City on December 15, 1913. Paul Fino attended public schools and graduated from St. Johns University School of Law in 1937. Fino was admitted to the New York State Bar in 1938 and began practice in New York City. He served as an assistant attorney general in state government from March 1943 to December 1944. Fino was a member of the New York State Senate from January 1945 to May 1950. He was then a member of the New York City Civil Service Commission from June 1, 1950, to December 31, 1952.

Fino was elected as a Republican to the 83rd and to seven succeeding Congresses. H served in the House of Representatives from January 3, 1953, until his resignation December 31, 1968, to become a New York Supreme Court Justice having been elected to that position November 5, 1968. During his time in the House, Fino was best known for trying to implement a national lottery. Fino assumed his duties as a New York Supreme Court Justice on January 1, 1969. Fino was a delegate to the New York Republican State Conventions from 1940 through 1966 and to the Republican National Conventions in 1960, 1964, and 1968. Paul Fino wrote the book My Life in Politics and Public Service (Great Neck, N.Y.: Todd and Honeywell, Inc., 1986). Fino resided in Atlantic Beach, New York until his death in 2009.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: This collection was processed by Sheri Sarnoff (2020), Kathy Merring-Darling (2023-2024) and Gareth Kaedy (2023-2024).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Paul A. Fino Papers include consituent files, legislative material, records relating to the national lottery that Fino tried to implement, subject files, and other records related to his time in the United States House of Representatives.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into four series. The legislation series is arranged by bill number while the other series are arranged alphabetically.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Paul Fino initially donated his papers to Syracuse University in 1968 and 1969. In 2006, the papers were transferred to the M.E. Grenander Department of Special Collections and Archives.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains the legislative records that Paul A. Fino worked with during his time in Congress from January 3, 1953 to December 31, 1968. During his time in the House of Representatives, he was a delegate to the Republican National Conventions in 1960, 1964, and 1968. During his time in office, Congressman Fino bills relating to a national lottery, veterans, tax relief (make tuition tax deductible), Social Security (increase benefits), historic preservation, gun legislation, and cigarette labeling (warn consumers of the dangers). Several bills such as those relating to Social Security, tax relief, and the lottery were sponsored multiple times over his career. This portion of the collection also contains correspondence regarding various bills from constituents and specific government departments and background research material.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This series is arranged alphanetically by last name.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains Paul A. Fino's constituent files from his time in the United States House of Representatives. Congressman Fino's constituents were mostly from the Bronx, New York, but some constituents in Brooklyn wrote to Congressman Fino because they did not have a Republican representative. This series contains correspondence from constituents divided into several categories: (service) academy, general, jobs, servicemen, veterans, and visas. Soldiers would often write to Congressman Fino and ask for help relating to hardship discharges, compassionate reassignments, medical discharges and transfers. While Congressman Fino did not have the authority to grant these assignments, he often had the contacts to help speed the process of receiving a response from the specified branches of the service. This series also includes records of constituents who asked Congressman Fino to recommend them for the United States Naval Academy, constituents asking for help them find a job, veterans asking for help related to Social Security and benefits, general questions about housing and government information, and constituents asking for assistance on behalf of family members to secure visas to immigrate to the United States. Congressman Fino also received requests asking for passes for tours of the White House, agricultural calendars, and flags that had flown over the Capitol.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains a variety of materials relating to Paul A. Fino's career as a Member of Congress. The materials within this series allow for one to see the breadth and scope of activities that Congressman Fino engaged in over his career. Within this series there is a large amount of correspondence from his constituents, letters pertaining to specific legislation, as well as that from departments within the government. In many cases Congressman Fino's reply is attached, whether it be a form letter or a specific response. Included in the subject files are Congressman Fino's remarks from the Congressional Record, relating to his position on other members' legislation, and press releases relating to specific bills he sponsored, which can be found within Series 1, entitled Legislation. Congressman Fino received numerous invitations during his time in office from constituents as well as to the inaugurations of Presidents Eisenhower and Kennedy which are located within folders entitled Inaugural Materials. This series also contains newspaper clippings, newsletters, and campaign materials from his own campaigns for the House and the Senate as well as those relating to presidential campaigns.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains Congressman Fino's efforts to establish a national and state lottery, with correspondence, newspaper and magazine articles, lottery bills, speeches, and press releases. Congressman Fino intended the lottery revenue to be used to pay the national deficit and promote a health care program. Congressman Fino wrote to many United States ambassadors across the globe asking for information regarding the amount of revenue earned from a national lottery in their respective postings. He received multiple replies with the ambassadors sending back not only the amount of revenue earned, but lottery tickets from around the globe. Congressman Fino also sought out the views of the American people regarding a national lottery. It was from this data that he argued for a decade for the institution of a national lottery.
